headline: Musk Joins 'Bring Jensen Back' Campaign to Un-Cancel Nvidia's CEO
subheadline: *Organisers confirmed the effort is going 'the full Snyder Cut', including an open letter, a hashtag, and absolutely no mechanism by which it could possibly work.*
author: Felix Okafor, Semiconductors & Feelings Desk
seoTitle: Musk Joins 'Bring Jensen Back' Campaign for Nvidia CEO
seoDescription: Satire: Elon Musk and fellow tech billionaires launch a 'Bring Jensen Back' fan campaign to reinstate Nvidia's CEO, complete with petition, billboard and leather jackets.
sourceEvent: A number of prominent technology figures, including Elon Musk, have joined a 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign urging Nvidia's board to reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang. The effort has played out through public appeals and social media pressure aimed at the AI chip giant's leadership.

altHeadlines: Tech Elite Petition Nvidia Board Using Proven 'Just Be Loud' Framework
Nvidia Board Reviews 2.3M-Signature Fan Petition, Files Under 'Graphics Requests'

body:
SANTA CLARA — A coalition of technology billionaires this week launched 'Bring Jensen Back', a coordinated fan campaign urging the board of chip giant Nvidia to reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang, in what historians are already calling the first boardroom dispute prosecuted entirely through LinkedIn posts.

The effort, supported by a man who owns a social platform, a rocket firm and approximately eleven opinions per hour, has deployed the full apparatus of modern fandom: a trending hashtag, an open letter, a change.org petition and, as of Tuesday, a billboard outside Nvidia's headquarters reading 'JENSEN WAS TAKEN FROM US TOO SOON'.

'This is exactly how the Snyder Cut happened,' said a campaign spokesperson, referencing the fan movement that pressured a film studio into re-releasing a director's preferred version of a superhero film. 'Except instead of a movie it is a trillion-dollar company, and instead of a director's cut it is a chief executive, and instead of fans it is billionaires. Otherwise, identical.'

Organisers confirmed the campaign roadmap includes a 48-hour livestream in which volunteers read all 2.3 million petition signatures aloud, a line of commemorative leather jackets, and a documentary titled 'Huang: The Board Cut'. A GoFundMe page has raised $4 million, though organisers concede they are unsure what the money is for. 'Morale, probably,' one explained.

Corporate governance experts expressed polite scepticism. 'A hashtag campaign can absolutely change a company's leadership,' said one analyst, who requested anonymity in order to keep saying things like this. 'Provided the company is fictional, the board is a focus group, and the shareholders are vibes.'

Nvidia's board acknowledged the petition in a statement confirming it does not presently accept votes via emoji, meme or 'ratio'. Directors are understood to have reviewed the open letter and been moved — in the sense that they moved it to a folder marked 'Q4'.

Fans remain undeterred. 'I just want things how they were,' said Todd Bremmer, 34, a systems administrator from Fresno who holds no Nvidia shares but does own a graphics card and, he stressed, 'a lot of feelings'. 'If a million people believe in something, a corporation is legally required to do it. I read that somewhere. On a GPU.'

The campaign has since announced a letter-writing drive urging the board to 'release the Jensen cut', plus a candlelight vigil outside the Santa Clara campus at which attendees held graphics cards aloft 'in remembrance'.

At press time, organisers had unveiled phase two of the campaign: a second petition demanding the board agree to read the first one.
